# claude-second-brain

> claude-second-brain is an open-source CLI (`npx claude-second-brain`) that scaffolds a personal knowledge base: a git repository that is also an Obsidian vault, where your AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and others) reads your sources and maintains a cross-linked wiki, searchable locally with qmd.

It is not a RAG system or a chatbot over your notes. The agent follows a schema file (`CLAUDE.md`, also reached through `AGENTS.md`) and a set of Agent Skills (`/brain-ingest`, `/brain-search`, `/brain-refresh`, `/brain-rebuild`, `/lint`) to summarize sources, update topic and entity pages, flag contradictions, and answer questions with citations. Every page below is also available as Markdown at the linked `.md` URL, and the whole site is in one file at `llms-full.txt`.

## Docs

- [claude-second-brain: CLI for an AI-maintained Obsidian knowledge base](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/index.md): claude-second-brain is an open-source CLI (npx claude-second-brain) that scaffolds a personal knowledge base: an Obsidian vault and git repo where your AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot) maintains a cross-linked wiki with local qmd search.
- [Getting Started](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/getting-started.md): Install and set up claude-second-brain in three steps: scaffold a brain with npx claude-second-brain, generate qmd vector embeddings, and open the folder as an Obsidian vault synced with git.
- [Commands](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli.md): Reference for the claude-second-brain CLI (alias csb): every command to create, list, switch and remove brains, install agent skills, run qmd, print paths, renew Cloudflare Artifacts git tokens, and run csb doctor.
- [csb](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/create.md): csb creates a new claude-second-brain: scaffolds the vault, installs dependencies, registers qmd collections, sets up a GitHub or Cloudflare Artifacts remote, and installs agent skills.
- [csb ls](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/ls.md): csb ls lists every claude-second-brain brain registered in config.toml with its path, creation date and git remote, and marks the default brain.
- [csb use](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/use.md): csb use sets the default claude-second-brain brain, which path, qmd, exec and the global agent skills resolve when no brain is named.
- [csb rm](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/rm.md): csb rm deletes one or more claude-second-brain brains and their config entries, and can also delete their GitHub or Cloudflare Artifacts remotes.
- [csb path](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/path.md): csb path prints the root directory, qmd index or config.toml path for the default or a named claude-second-brain brain, so scripts and skills work from anywhere.
- [csb qmd](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/qmd.md): csb qmd runs the qmd search CLI against the default or a named claude-second-brain brain, with INDEX_PATH and the working directory already set.
- [csb exec](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/exec.md): csb exec runs any command inside the default or a named claude-second-brain brain's directory with INDEX_PATH set, for vault-local scripts like pnpm qmd:reindex.
- [csb skills](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/skills.md): csb skills installs or updates the claude-second-brain Agent Skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and 11 more agents, using the same layout as npx skills.
- [csb git-token](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/git-token.md): csb git-token mints a new Cloudflare Artifacts git token for a claude-second-brain brain and saves it in the vault's .git/config so git push and pull work again.
- [csb doctor](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/doctor.md): csb doctor checks the tools, config.toml, registered brains, qmd indexes and installed agent skills that claude-second-brain needs, and prints a fix for each problem.
- [How it works](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/concepts/how-it-works.md): How claude-second-brain works: raw sources flow through your AI agent into a cross-linked wiki, qmd indexes every page for hybrid search, and git syncs the vault to Obsidian and every device.
- [Wiki schema](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/concepts/schema.md): The wiki schema your agent follows: directory layout, page types, YAML frontmatter fields, naming and wikilink rules, contradiction callouts, and the hard rules from CLAUDE.md.
- [GitHub remote](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/github.md): Use a private GitHub repository as the git backend for your claude-second-brain vault, with version history, access from any device, and Obsidian mobile sync.
- [Cloudflare Artifacts remote](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/cloudflare-artifacts.md): Use Cloudflare Artifacts as a git-compatible remote for your claude-second-brain vault, so your notes never touch GitHub. Covers setup, tokens, and csb git-token.
- [Skills](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills.md): The Agent Skills that run the claude-second-brain wiki in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot and other agents: ingest, search, refresh, rebuild and lint, plus how to install and update them.
- [/brain-ingest](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-ingest.md): The /brain-ingest skill: read a new source, write a source summary page, update affected topic and entity pages, flag contradictions, and log the change.
- [/brain-search](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-search.md): The /brain-search skill: query the wiki with qmd hybrid search, read the top pages, answer with [[wikilink]] citations, and optionally file the answer as a Q&A page.
- [/brain-refresh](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-refresh.md): The /brain-refresh skill: rescan the vault and regenerate qmd embeddings for new or changed files, or re-embed everything with force.
- [/brain-rebuild](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-rebuild.md): The /brain-rebuild skill (destructive): propose a new qmd collection and context schema, then drop and rebuild the search index from scratch after approval.
- [/lint](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/lint.md): The /lint skill: health-check the wiki for orphan pages, broken wikilinks, unresolved contradictions, stale claims, missing pages and data gaps, and fix what is safe.

## Project

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain): Source code, issues, the `CLAUDE.md` schema, and the template vault copied on scaffold
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/claude-second-brain): The published CLI. Run `npx claude-second-brain` with no global install
- [Full docs in one file](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/llms-full.txt): Every docs page concatenated as Markdown

- [Ship log](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/ship-log.md): Release history for the claude-second-brain npm package and its agent skills, newest first.

# Your notes don't compound. claude-second-brain turns them into a wiki that does.

Scaffold a personal knowledge base: an Obsidian vault and git repo where your AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and more) reads your sources and maintains a cross-linked wiki with local qmd search.

```bash
npx claude-second-brain
```

[Get started](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/getting-started) · Want the details first? [How it works](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/concepts/how-it-works) · [CLI reference](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli) · [GitHub](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain)

One command gives you a fully wired knowledge system:

* **Your AI agent** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …) ingests your sources and maintains a cross-linked wiki
* **qmd** powers local semantic search (vector + BM25)
* The scaffolded folder **is your Obsidian vault** — open it directly, with [obsidian-git](https://github.com/Vinzent03/obsidian-git) pre-configured for seamless sync
* **Git** ([GitHub](https://github.com), [Cloudflare Artifacts](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/), or any remote) is the source of truth — version history, anywhere access, and a backup you control

You've been reading papers, articles, and books for years. Drop a source in, run [`/brain-ingest`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-ingest), and your agent reads it — extracts what matters, cross-links it to everything you already know, and files it. Ask a question six months later and get cited answers, not a list of files to re-read.

> Inspired by [Andrej Karpathy's approach to LLM-powered knowledge management](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2040470801506541998?s=20) — share an "idea file" with an LLM agent and let it build and maintain your knowledge base.

## How this is different

This is not a RAG system. It's not a chatbot over your notes. It's an actively maintained, cross-linked wiki — five structured page types, YAML frontmatter, and a set of [agent skills](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills) — usable from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, or any agent that supports [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) — that run the whole thing.

The schema ([CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)) is that idea file. Your agent reads it every session (other agents reach it through `AGENTS.md`).

## The stack

| Tool | Role |
| --- | --- |
| **Your agent** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, …) | Reads sources, writes wiki pages, cross-links, flags contradictions |
| **qmd** | Local hybrid search (vector + BM25) across your entire wiki |
| **Obsidian** | Graph view, backlinks, mobile reading — offline, no extra sync |
| **Git** (GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts, …) | Source of truth — version history, your agent anywhere, Obsidian sync |

Everything is pre-configured. You bring the sources.

Next: [Get started in 3 steps →](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/getting-started)

<!-- Source: /getting-started -->

# Getting Started

## Requirements

* [pnpm](https://pnpm.io) 10+ on Node 22+, or [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) — if pnpm isn't installed, the CLI installs mise and uses it to fetch node + pnpm
* An AI coding agent that supports [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) — [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code), Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Goose, … Setup asks which ones to install the skills for.
* [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md/) — optional but recommended

## Step 1 — Scaffold

```bash
npx claude-second-brain
```

Or install globally for a shorter command (`csb` is an alias):

```bash
npm i -g claude-second-brain
csb                    # same as: claude-second-brain
```

The CLI will ask:

* **Brain name** — what to call this brain (default: `my-brain`)
* **Git remote** — optionally host your vault on **[GitHub](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/github)** (requires `gh` CLI) or **[Cloudflare Artifacts](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/cloudflare-artifacts)** (requires a Cloudflare account + wrangler)
* **Register qmd collections after install?** — runs `pnpm qmd:setup` once dependencies are installed
* **Install skills for which agents?** — Claude Code plus any detected agent is preselected; see [Install skills for any agent](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/skills#install-skills-for-any-agent)

Every question is asked up front, so the rest of setup runs unattended.

Creates the brain at `~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/`, registers it in `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml`, runs `pnpm install` (using your system pnpm 10+, or mise to fetch node + pnpm if it's missing), registers the qmd collections, installs the skills for the agents you picked, and runs `git init`.

## Step 2 — Generate vector embeddings

```bash
cd ~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain && pnpm qmd:reindex
```

Generates local vector embeddings. First run downloads ~2GB of GGUF models — once.

## Step 3 — Open in Obsidian (and push to GitHub if not done)

**If you created a GitHub repo during setup**, it's already pushed — skip straight to opening in Obsidian.

**If you skipped GitHub during setup**, connect it now:

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/you/my-brain.git
git push -u origin main
```

Open `~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/` as a vault in Obsidian — the folder is already a valid Obsidian vault. The Git plugin is pre-configured — enable it and sync is automatic.

## Multiple brains

Run `npx claude-second-brain` (or `csb` if installed globally) again to create additional brains. Each gets its own folder under `~/.claude-second-brain/` and its own isolated qmd index. The global skills (`/brain-ingest`, `/brain-search`, `/brain-refresh`) always operate on the **default brain** in `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml`. The first brain created is set as the default automatically.

See the [CLI Reference](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli) for `ls`, `use`, `rm`, `path`, `qmd`, `exec`, `skills`, `git-token`, and `doctor` subcommands that manage and target specific brains.

## Access from anywhere

**Edit anywhere — your agent on desktop, web or mobile.** The vault is a plain git repo, so any agent that can clone it can work on it: run it locally, or use a cloud agent with GitHub access (Claude Code on the web and mobile, Codex cloud, Copilot coding agent, Cursor background agents, …) to ingest a source, run a query, or update a page from your phone.

**Read anywhere — Obsidian desktop and mobile.** Open the repo as an Obsidian vault. The bundled `.obsidian` folder pre-configures [obsidian-git](https://github.com/Vinzent03/obsidian-git) — no setup required. Your wiki syncs automatically on every commit. For iOS: put the repo folder inside iCloud Drive — Obsidian Mobile picks it up natively.

**Browse anywhere — your git host.** It's a plain git repo. On GitHub (or any host with a web UI), view and edit files directly in the browser at any time.

<!-- Source: /cli -->

# Commands

The `claude-second-brain` CLI creates and manages brains registered in `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml`.

## Usage

Run it without installing anything:

:::code-group
```bash [npm]
npx claude-second-brain
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm dlx claude-second-brain
```

```bash [bun]
bunx claude-second-brain
```
:::

### Global install

Install it globally to get the shorter `csb` alias. Every page in this reference uses `csb`; substitute `npx claude-second-brain` if you haven't installed it.

:::code-group
```bash [npm]
npm install -g claude-second-brain
csb ls
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add -g claude-second-brain
csb ls
```

```bash [bun]
bun add -g claude-second-brain
csb ls
```
:::

## Available commands

* [`csb [<name>]`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/create): Create a new brain. Interactive unless you pass a name and flags.
* [`csb ls`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/ls): List all registered brains. The default brain is marked with `*`.
* [`csb use <name>`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/use): Set the default brain.
* [`csb rm [<name>…]`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/rm): Delete one or more brains, and optionally their remotes.
* [`csb path [qmd|config|root]`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/path): Print a path for the default (or named) brain.
* [`csb qmd <qmd args…>`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/qmd): Run `qmd` against the default (or named) brain.
* [`csb exec -- <cmd…>`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/exec): Run a command inside the default (or named) brain's directory.
* [`csb skills`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/skills): Install or update the wiki skills for any agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, …).
* [`csb git-token [<name>]`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/git-token): Renew the git push/pull token for a [Cloudflare Artifacts](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/cloudflare-artifacts) brain.
* [`csb doctor`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/doctor): Verify your setup and suggest fixes.

`ls` is also available as `list`, `rm` as `remove`, and `use` as `default` or `switch`.

## Display info

### `-h`, `--help`

Show usage. Works on its own, after any command, or as `csb help <command>`.

```bash
csb --help
csb rm --help
csb help qmd
```

## Environment variables

| Variable | Description |
|---|---|
| `CSB_AGENTS` | Agents to install skills for, comma-separated or `all`. Used by [`csb`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/create) and [`csb skills`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/skills) when `--agent` is not passed. |
| `CSB_USE_MISE` | Set to `1` to always fetch node and pnpm with mise, even if pnpm 10+ is on your `PATH`. |
| `CSB_ICONS` | `nerd`, `emoji` or `none`: icons in the git-remote picker. Nerd Font logos are on by default in Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty. |
| `CSB_SKIP_SKILL_UPDATES` | Set to `1` to update outdated global skills without prompting. |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | API token with Artifacts Read and Edit. Used instead of your `wrangler` login. |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | Cloudflare account to use when your login can see more than one. |
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | Where Claude Code reads its config. Skills for Claude Code go in its `skills/` folder. |

## Exit status

Every command exits non-zero on failure (an unknown brain name, a missing config, a failed `doctor` check, a remote that could not be created) and writes the error to stderr.

<!-- Source: /cli/create -->

# csb

Create a new brain.

## Usage

```bash
csb [<name>] [--agent <ids>] [--copy]
```

Creates the brain at `~/.claude-second-brain/<name>/`, runs `pnpm install`, `pnpm qmd:setup` and `git init`, and registers it in `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml`. The first brain you create becomes the default.

## Arguments

### name

`string`

Name of the brain. Skips the name prompt. Defaults to `my-brain` when you accept the prompt's suggestion.

```bash
csb my-brain
```

## Options

### -a, --agent \<ids>

`string`

Agents to install skills for, comma-separated, or `all`. Also read from `CSB_AGENTS`. Without it, the CLI prompts (interactive) or uses Claude Code plus every detected agent (non-interactive). See [`csb skills`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/skills) for the agent IDs.

```bash
csb my-brain --agent claude-code,codex
```

### --copy

`boolean`

Copy skills into each agent's folder instead of symlinking them to `~/.agents/skills`.

```bash
csb my-brain --copy
```

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb --help
```

## Prompts

All questions are asked up front, so the rest of setup runs unattended:

| Prompt | Default | Shown when |
|---|---|---|
| Brain name | `my-brain` | No `name` argument |
| Git remote | none | Always: `GitHub`, `Cloudflare Artifacts` or `Skip` |
| Repo name | the brain name | A remote is selected |
| Artifacts namespace | `default` | Cloudflare Artifacts is selected |
| Register qmd collections after install? | yes | Always |
| Install skills for which agents? | Claude Code plus detected agents | No `--agent` and no `CSB_AGENTS` |

See [GitHub](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/github) and [Cloudflare Artifacts](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/cloudflare-artifacts) for what each remote needs.

## Behavior

* Long steps show a spinner with elapsed time and the latest output line.
* If `pnpm` 10+ is already on your `PATH`, it is used directly. Otherwise the CLI installs mise (if needed) and runs `mise install` to fetch node and pnpm first. Set `CSB_USE_MISE=1` to always use mise.
* `CSB_ICONS=nerd|emoji|none` picks the icons in the git-remote picker. Real GitHub and Cloudflare logos (Nerd Font glyphs) are on by default in Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty. Set `CSB_ICONS=nerd` in other terminals if you use a Nerd Font.
* The closing **Next steps** box shows how to open each agent you picked (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor .`, …).
* If the GitHub or Cloudflare remote can't be created or pushed, the brain is still created locally, **Next steps** lists the fix, and the CLI exits 1.

<!-- Source: /cli/ls -->

# csb ls

List all registered brains.

## Usage

```bash
csb ls
```

Alias: `csb list`.

Prints each brain in `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml` with its path, creation date and git remote. The default brain is shown in bold with a `*` marker.

## Options

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb ls --help
```

<!-- Source: /cli/use -->

# csb use

Set the default brain.

## Usage

```bash
csb use <name>
```

Aliases: `csb default`, `csb switch`.

Rewrites the `default = "…"` line in `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml`. Every later command that resolves the default brain uses the new one: [`csb path`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/path), [`csb qmd`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/qmd), [`csb exec`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/exec), and the global skills (`/brain-ingest`, `/brain-search`, `/brain-refresh`).

## Arguments

### name

`string` (required)

A registered brain. Errors if the name isn't registered; run [`csb ls`](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/ls) to see the available names.

```bash
csb use work
```

## Options

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb use --help
```

<!-- Source: /cli/rm -->

# csb rm

Remove one or more brains.

## Usage

```bash
csb rm [<name>…] [-y] [--delete-remote | --keep-remote]
```

Alias: `csb remove`.

Deletes each brain's directory under `~/.claude-second-brain/` and removes its entry from `config.toml`. If you remove the default brain and others remain, the first remaining brain becomes the new default.

## Arguments

### name

`string[]`

One or more brains to remove. Without a name, the CLI shows a multi-select picker: press **space** to toggle a brain, **a** to toggle all, **enter** to confirm.

```bash
csb rm a b c
```

## Options

### -y, --yes

`boolean`

Skip the confirmation prompt. On its own it keeps remotes (safe default).

```bash
csb rm my-brain --yes
```

### --delete-remote

`boolean`

Also delete each brain's remote, without prompting. Can't be combined with `--keep-remote`.

```bash
csb rm a b --yes --delete-remote
```

### --keep-remote

`boolean`

Keep each brain's remote, without prompting.

```bash
csb rm a b --yes --keep-remote
```

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb rm --help
```

## Remote deletion

For each brain with a registered `git_remote`, the CLI can also delete the remote repo:

* **GitHub**: runs `gh repo delete <owner>/<repo> --yes` (needs the `gh` CLI with the `delete_repo` scope).
* **Cloudflare Artifacts**: calls `DELETE https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/artifacts/namespaces/<ns>/repos/<repo>` with `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` or a token from `wrangler auth token`.

| Flags | Remotes |
|---|---|
| none (interactive) | Prompts per brain |
| `--keep-remote` | Kept, no prompt |
| `--delete-remote` | Deleted, no prompt |
| `-y` without a remote flag | Kept |

If a remote deletion fails (missing CLI, revoked token, …), the CLI prints the exact manual command and continues. The local directory and config entry are still removed.

<!-- Source: /cli/path -->

# csb path

Print a path for the default (or named) brain.

## Usage

```bash
csb path [root|qmd|config] [--brain <name>]
```

The global skills (`/brain-ingest`, `/brain-search`, `/brain-refresh`) call this to resolve paths at run time, so they work from any working directory.

## Arguments

### kind

`'root' | 'qmd' | 'config'` (default: `'root'`)

| Value | Prints |
|---|---|
| `root` | The brain's directory, e.g. `~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain` |
| `qmd` | The brain's qmd SQLite index, e.g. `~/.claude-second-brain/my-brain/.qmd/index.sqlite` |
| `config` | The central `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml`. Ignores `--brain`. |

```bash
csb path qmd
```

## Options

### --brain \<name>

`string`

Target a specific brain instead of the default.

```bash
csb path qmd --brain work
```

### --root, --qmd, --config

`boolean` (deprecated)

Old flag form of the `kind` argument. Still works, and prints a warning to stderr.

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb path --help
```

<!-- Source: /cli/qmd -->

# csb qmd

Run [qmd](https://github.com/tobi/qmd) against the default (or named) brain.

## Usage

```bash
csb qmd [--brain <name>] [--] <qmd args…>
```

Forwards every argument that isn't a `csb` flag to `npx @tobilu/qmd`, with `INDEX_PATH` set to the brain's qmd index and the working directory set to the brain's root.

## Arguments

### qmd args

`string[]`

Passed to qmd as is.

```bash
csb qmd query -c wiki "distributed systems"
```

## Options

### --brain \<name>

`string`

Target a specific brain instead of the default.

```bash
csb qmd --brain work search -c wiki "kafka"
```

### --

Optional separator. Everything after it goes to qmd verbatim. Use it only to pass a literal `--brain` (or another `csb` flag) through to qmd.

```bash
csb qmd -- --brain literal-qmd-flag
```

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb qmd --help
```

<!-- Source: /cli/exec -->

# csb exec

Run a command inside the default (or named) brain's directory.

## Usage

```bash
csb exec [--brain <name>] -- <cmd…>
```

Sets `INDEX_PATH` to the brain's qmd index and the working directory to the brain's root, then runs the command. Useful for vault-local scripts that assume you're in the brain root.

## Arguments

### cmd

`string[]` (required)

The command to run and its arguments, after `--`.

```bash
csb exec -- pnpm qmd:reindex
```

## Options

### --brain \<name>

`string`

Target a specific brain instead of the default.

```bash
csb exec --brain work -- git status
```

### --

Required separator before the command to run.

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb exec --help
```

<!-- Source: /cli/skills -->

# csb skills

Install or update the wiki skills for any agent.

## Usage

```bash
csb skills [--agent <ids>] [--copy] [--brain <name>]
csb skills --list
```

The skills follow the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/specification) format and are installed with the same layout as [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills). See [Install skills for any agent](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/skills#install-skills-for-any-agent) below.

## Options

### -a, --agent \<ids>

`string` (default: `claude-code` plus detected agents)

Agents to install for, comma-separated, or `all`. Also read from `CSB_AGENTS`. Without either, the CLI prompts (interactive) or uses Claude Code plus every detected agent (non-interactive).

```bash
csb skills --agent codex,cursor
```

### --copy

`boolean`

Copy skills into each agent's folder instead of symlinking them to `~/.agents/skills`.

```bash
csb skills --agent all --copy
```

### --brain \<name>

`string`

Brain whose vault-local skills to update. Defaults to the default brain.

```bash
csb skills --brain work
```

### --list

`boolean`

List the supported agents and where each reads skills.

```bash
csb skills --list
```

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb skills --help
```

## Install skills for any agent

* **Global skills** (`brain-ingest`, `brain-search`, `brain-refresh`) are written once to `~/.agents/skills/<name>`, with a `.csb-version` marker. Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Amp and Cline read `~/.agents/skills` directly.
* Agents with their own folder get a **symlink** to the shared copy: `~/.claude/skills` (Claude Code, honours `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`), `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills`, `~/.config/goose/skills`, `~/.kiro/skills`, `~/.roo/skills`, `~/.continue/skills`, `~/.junie/skills`, `~/.augment/skills`. If a symlink can't be created, or with `--copy`, the skill is copied instead.
* **Vault-local skills** (`brain-rebuild`, `lint`) stay in the vault's `.claude/skills/` and are copied (never symlinked, since the vault is a git repo) into each other selected agent's project folder (`.agents/skills/`, `.windsurf/skills/`, …) of the default brain, or the one named with `--brain`. Commit them to sync.

Agents are detected by their config folder (e.g. `~/.codex`, `~/.cursor`, `~/.copilot`). Upgrading from a release that installed only to `~/.claude/skills`: run `csb skills` once, and existing copies there are replaced with symlinks to `~/.agents/skills`.

## Supported agents

| ID | Agent | Project skills dir | Global skills dir |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-code` | Claude Code | `.claude/skills` | `~/.claude/skills` |
| `codex` | Codex | `.agents/skills` | `~/.agents/skills` |
| `cursor` | Cursor | `.agents/skills` | `~/.agents/skills` |
| `gemini-cli` | Gemini CLI | `.agents/skills` | `~/.agents/skills` |
| `github-copilot` | GitHub Copilot | `.agents/skills` | `~/.agents/skills` |
| `opencode` | OpenCode | `.agents/skills` | `~/.agents/skills` |
| `amp` | Amp | `.agents/skills` | `~/.agents/skills` |
| `cline` | Cline | `.agents/skills` | `~/.agents/skills` |
| `windsurf` | Windsurf | `.windsurf/skills` | `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills` |
| `goose` | Goose | `.goose/skills` | `~/.config/goose/skills` |
| `kiro-cli` | Kiro CLI | `.kiro/skills` | `~/.kiro/skills` |
| `roo` | Roo Code | `.roo/skills` | `~/.roo/skills` |
| `continue` | Continue | `.continue/skills` | `~/.continue/skills` |
| `junie` | Junie | `.junie/skills` | `~/.junie/skills` |
| `augment` | Augment | `.augment/skills` | `~/.augment/skills` |

<!-- Source: /cli/git-token -->

# csb git-token

Renew the git token for a [Cloudflare Artifacts](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/cloudflare-artifacts) brain.

## Usage

```bash
csb git-token [<name>] [--ttl <duration>] [--read] [--print]
```

Artifacts git tokens expire. This mints a new repo-scoped token with your `wrangler` login (or `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) and saves it as `http.<remote>.extraHeader` in the brain's `.git/config` (local only, never committed), so plain `git push` / `git pull` and obsidian-git work again. See [Renewing the git token](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/remotes/cloudflare-artifacts#renewing-the-git-token).

## Arguments

### name

`string`

Brain to renew. Defaults to the default brain. Same as `--brain`.

```bash
csb git-token my-brain
```

## Options

### --brain \<name>

`string`

Brain to renew, as a flag.

```bash
csb git-token --brain my-brain
```

### --ttl \<duration>

`string` (default: `90d`)

Token lifetime: seconds, or `12h`, `90d`, `1y`. Maximum 1 year.

```bash
csb git-token --ttl 1y
```

### --read

`boolean`

Mint a read-only token instead of a write token.

```bash
csb git-token --read
```

### --print

`boolean`

Print the token instead of saving it, for example to use on another machine.

```bash
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Bearer $(csb git-token --print)" pull
```

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb git-token --help
```

<!-- Source: /cli/doctor -->

# csb doctor

Verify your setup and suggest fixes.

## Usage

```bash
csb doctor
```

## Checks

* Installed tools: `gh` (and its auth status), `mise` or `pnpm` 10+, and `wrangler` (optional).
* A parseable `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml`.
* At least one registered brain, and a default brain that resolves.
* For each brain: the `path` directory and the `qmd_index` file exist.
* Each global skill is installed in `~/.agents/skills` at this release's version.

Each failed or warning check prints a `Fix:` hint with the exact command to run. Exits non-zero when a check fails.

## Options

### -h, --help

Displays help message.

```bash
csb doctor --help
```

<!-- Source: /concepts/how-it-works -->

# How it works

Sources go in on the left, your agent synthesizes them into the wiki, qmd indexes every page into a local hybrid search index, and git makes the whole vault editable from Obsidian and your agent on any device.

Articles, PDFs, notes and your questions go in through your agent; the wiki and its qmd index sit in the middle; Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Obsidian and git all read and edit the same vault. Your agent runs /brain-ingest on new sources and /brain-search on questions; qmd indexes every page; git keeps every device in sync.

**You bring:**

* Articles
* PDFs
* Personal notes
* Questions

**In the middle:** Your wiki (wiki/ + qmd index)

**Works with:**

* Claude Code
* Codex
* Cursor
* Obsidian
* Git remote

## The ingest loop, zoomed in

```
┌─────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐        ┌─────────────────────┐
│   Drop in a source  │        │ /brain-ingest       │        │     Wiki grows      │
│                     │        │                     │        │                     │
│  · article          │──────▶ │  reads + extracts   │──────▶ │  · cross-linked     │
│  · PDF              │        │  key knowledge      │        │  · contradictions   │
│  · personal note    │        │                     │        │    flagged          │
│                     │        │                     │        │  · syntheses        │
└─────────────────────┘        └─────────────────────┘        └─────────────────────┘
```

Query it anytime with `/brain-search`. Get answers with inline `[[wiki/page]]` citations, not a list of files.

## Directory layout

```
my-brain/
├── CLAUDE.md              ← The schema. Your agent reads this every session.
├── raw-sources/           ← Your raw inputs. The agent never modifies these.
│   ├── articles/
│   ├── pdfs/
│   └── personal/
├── wiki/                  ← The agent owns this entirely.
│   ├── index.md
│   ├── log.md
│   ├── overview.md
│   ├── sources/
│   └── qa/
└── scripts/qmd/           ← Semantic search setup and re-indexing
```

<!-- Source: /concepts/schema -->

# Wiki schema

The authoritative schema lives in [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) — your agent reads it at the start of every session (agents that look for `AGENTS.md` are pointed to it). This page is a readable summary.

## Page types

| Type | File | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `overview` | `wiki/overview.md` | Evolving high-level synthesis |
| `topic` | `wiki/[concept].md` | A concept, domain, or idea |
| `entity` | `wiki/[name].md` | A person, tool, company, or project |
| `source-summary` | `wiki/sources/[slug].md` | One page per ingested source |
| `qa` | `wiki/qa/[slug].md` | Filed answers to notable queries |

Plus two admin pages: `wiki/index.md` (master index) and `wiki/log.md` (running activity log).

## Frontmatter

Every wiki page has YAML frontmatter:

```yaml
---
type: overview | topic | entity | source-summary | qa | admin
tags: [tag1, tag2]
sources: ["[[wiki/sources/source-slug]]"]
related: ["[[wiki/related-page]]"]
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

## Naming conventions

* **File names** — kebab-case, all lowercase. `machine-learning-ops.md`, not `MachineLearningOps.md`.
* **Links** — always Obsidian `[[wikilinks]]` for internal cross-references. Full paths from vault root: `[[wiki/distributed-systems]]`.
* **Sections** — `##` for top-level, `###` for subsections.
* **Contradictions** — flagged with a `> [!WARNING] Contradiction` callout. Both claims and their sources are stated.
* **Uncertainty** — claims the model isn't sure about are marked with `[?]` inline.

## Directory layout

```
my-brain/
├── CLAUDE.md              ← The schema
├── raw-sources/           ← Immutable raw inputs
│   ├── articles/
│   ├── pdfs/
│   └── personal/
└── wiki/                  ← Agent-owned knowledge base
    ├── index.md
    ├── log.md
    ├── overview.md
    ├── sources/
    └── qa/
```

## Hard rules

1. Nothing in `raw-sources/` is ever modified — they are immutable raw inputs.
2. Only `wiki/` is owned by the agent; the rest of the vault is untouched.
3. `wiki/log.md` is append-only, never overwritten.
4. One source summary per ingested source in `wiki/sources/` — never merged.
5. Every wiki page has frontmatter with at least `type` and `updated`.
6. Cross-link aggressively — if a topic has (or should have) a page, link it with `[[wiki/page]]`.
7. Pages are **synthesis**, not transcription.

<!-- Source: /remotes/github -->

# GitHub remote

GitHub is the default Git backend for claude-second-brain. Your vault is stored as a private GitHub repository — you get version history, access from any device, and Obsidian mobile sync via the bundled Git plugin.

## Prerequisites

* A [GitHub account](https://github.com/join)
* [`gh` CLI](https://cli.github.com/) — used for authentication and repo creation during setup

## Setup (automatic)

When you run `npx claude-second-brain` and select **GitHub** as your remote, the CLI handles everything:

1. Checks `gh auth status` — runs `gh auth login` if not authenticated
2. Creates a private repo: `gh repo create <name> --private --source=. --remote=origin --push`
3. Pushes the initial commit

## Manual setup

If you skipped GitHub during setup, or `gh` wasn't installed, connect it manually:

```bash
# With gh CLI
gh repo create my-brain --private --source=. --remote=origin --push

# Without gh CLI
git remote add origin https://github.com/you/my-brain.git
git push -u origin main
```

## Syncing from Obsidian

The vault includes a pre-configured `.obsidian/` folder with [obsidian-git](https://github.com/Vinzent03/obsidian-git) settings. Enable the plugin in Obsidian → Community plugins and it will auto-commit and push on a schedule.

For iOS: place the repo folder inside iCloud Drive — Obsidian Mobile picks it up natively and obsidian-git handles sync.

<!-- Source: /remotes/cloudflare-artifacts -->

# Cloudflare Artifacts remote

[Cloudflare Artifacts](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/) is a git-compatible object storage remote. It's a good choice if you don't want to use GitHub — your vault data stays on Cloudflare's infrastructure and never touches GitHub.

## Prerequisites

* A [Cloudflare account](https://dash.cloudflare.com/sign-up) on the **Workers Paid** plan (required for Artifacts)
* Either `wrangler login` (the CLI runs it for you and requests `artifacts:write`), or `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` set to an [API token](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/api/get-started/create-token/) with **Artifacts › Read** and **Artifacts › Edit**
* If your login can see more than one account, set `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` (or pick it when prompted)
* `wrangler` CLI — if not installed, the setup wizard falls back to `npx wrangler` automatically

## Setup (automatic)

When you run `npx claude-second-brain` and select **Cloudflare Artifacts** as your remote, the CLI handles everything:

1. Checks wrangler auth (logs you in and requests the `artifacts:write` scope if needed)
2. Resolves your account ID and creates a new Artifacts repo via the [Artifacts REST API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/api/rest-api/) (`api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/artifacts/…`)
3. Runs `git remote add origin <remote-url>`
4. Pushes the initial commit
5. Mints a 90-day git token and saves it in the vault's `.git/config`, so `git push` / `git pull` just work

## Manual setup

If you skipped Cloudflare Artifacts during setup, or setup failed, you can connect an existing brain by hand. These are the same [REST API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/api/rest-api/) calls the CLI makes:

```bash
# 1. Credentials: a wrangler login token (or your own CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) and your account ID
export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN="${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN:-$(npx wrangler auth token)}"
export CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=<your-account-id>   # shown by `npx wrangler whoami`
API=https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID/artifacts

# 2. Create the namespace (skip if it already exists)
curl -s -X POST "$API/namespaces" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"namespace":"default"}'

# 3. Create the repo. The response's result.remote is the git URL and result.token a 24-hour push token
curl -s -X POST "$API/namespaces/default/repos" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"my-brain","default_branch":"main"}'

# 4. From the vault root: add the remote and push with that token
git remote add origin <result.remote>   # https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.artifacts.cloudflare.net/git/default/my-brain.git
git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Bearer <result.token>" push -u origin main

# 5. Save a 90-day token so plain git push / git pull (and obsidian-git) work
csb git-token my-brain
```

To remove the repo later: `curl -X DELETE "$API/namespaces/default/repos/my-brain" -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN"`.

## Renewing the git token

Artifacts git tokens expire (csb mints them for 90 days; Cloudflare allows up to 1 year). When `git push` or `git pull` starts failing with an auth error, renew it:

```bash
csb git-token            # default brain
csb git-token my-brain   # a specific brain
```

This mints a new repo-scoped token with your wrangler login (or `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`) and stores it for the brain's remote as `http.<remote>.extraHeader` in the vault's `.git/config` — local only, never committed. Plain `git push` / `git pull` (and obsidian-git) work again until it expires.

Options: `--ttl <duration>` for a different lifetime (seconds, or `12h`, `90d`, `1y`; max 1 year), `--read` for a read-only token, `--print` to print the token instead of saving it (e.g. for another machine: `git -c http.extraHeader="Authorization: Bearer $(csb git-token --print)" pull`).

## Namespace

During setup, the CLI asks for an **Artifacts namespace** (default: `default`). Namespaces scope repos within your Cloudflare account — useful if you manage multiple projects. For personal use, the default is fine.

## If setup fails

If the repo can't be created or the first push fails, the CLI still creates the brain locally but says so in a warning, lists the fix in **Next steps**, and exits non-zero. A `403` / `Authentication error` usually means Artifacts isn't enabled on the account (Workers Paid plan), the token is missing the Artifacts permission, or `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` points at another account. A `404` / `Namespace is not active` means the namespace was deleted; the CLI recreates it and retries automatically, and if that still fails, wait a minute (deletion can take a moment to finish) or pick another namespace. Fix it, then `csb rm <name>` and re-run, or add any other git remote by hand.

<!-- Source: /skills -->

# Skills

The wiki ships with a set of [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) that cover the full workflow, and they work in any agent that supports skills: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Goose and more. No manual prompting, no copy-pasting.

## Daily workflow

* [**`/brain-ingest`**](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-ingest) — Drop a file into `raw-sources/`. Your agent summarizes the source, creates a `wiki/sources/` page, updates related topic pages, and flags contradictions.
* [**`/brain-search`**](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-search) — Ask anything. Your agent runs hybrid search, reads the most relevant pages, and writes an answer with inline `[[wiki/page]]` citations.
* [**`/lint`**](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/lint) — Health-check the wiki. Surfaces orphan pages, broken links, unresolved contradictions, and data gaps.

## Maintenance

* [**`/brain-refresh`**](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-refresh) — Re-scan the vault and regenerate vector embeddings for new or changed files.
* [**`/brain-rebuild`**](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/skills/brain-rebuild) — **Destructive.** Redesigns the qmd schema, drops the old index, and rebuilds from scratch. Use only when the current structure no longer fits how you search.

## Install or update skills

The skills follow the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io/specification) format, so they work in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Goose and more. `/brain-ingest`, `/brain-search`, and `/brain-refresh` install globally during setup — once to `~/.agents/skills/`, with symlinks from agent-specific folders like `~/.claude/skills/`. `/brain-rebuild` and `/lint` live inside the vault at `.claude/skills/` and are copied to `.agents/skills/` and other agents' folders for the agents you pick.

To install for more agents later, or after upgrading the CLI:

```bash
npx claude-second-brain skills --agent codex,cursor,github-copilot
```

See [Install skills for any agent](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain/pr-preview/pr-32/cli/skills#install-skills-for-any-agent) for the full layout.

To pull in improvements from the latest template:

```bash
# Install or update all 5 wiki skills
npx skills add https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/tree/main/template/.claude/skills -a claude-code -y

# Or update a specific skill
npx skills add https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/tree/main/template/.claude/skills --skill brain-ingest -a claude-code -y
```

Once installed via `npx skills`, future updates are a single command:

```bash
npx skills update -a claude-code
```

<!-- Source: /skills/brain-ingest -->

# /brain-ingest

Ingest a new source into the wiki.

Drop a file into `raw-sources/articles/`, `raw-sources/pdfs/`, or `raw-sources/personal/`, then run `/brain-ingest`. Your agent will:

1. **Read** the source in full.
2. **Summarize** it in 3–5 bullets and ask you what matters most.
3. **Create** a `wiki/sources/[slug].md` page with abstract, key claims, notable quotes, and your synthesis note.
4. **Update** or create topic/entity pages that the source touches, integrating it as prose (not copy-paste) with source attribution.
5. **Flag contradictions** with `[!WARNING]` callouts on any page where the new source disagrees with existing claims.
6. **Log** the ingest in `wiki/log.md`.

Scope: global skill, installed once at `~/.agents/skills/brain-ingest/SKILL.md` and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/brain-ingest`). Paths resolve at call time via `npx claude-second-brain path` and `npx claude-second-brain qmd` — both read `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml` to find the default brain. Source: [template/.claude/skills/brain-ingest/SKILL.md](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/blob/main/template/.claude/skills/brain-ingest/SKILL.md).

<!-- Source: /skills/brain-search -->

# /brain-search

Query the wiki to answer a question.

Runs hybrid search (vector + BM25) across the entire wiki, reads the 2–5 most relevant pages, and synthesizes an answer with inline `[[wiki/page]]` citations. Flags gaps where the wiki has no coverage.

If the answer pulls together multiple pages in a novel way, it offers to file it as a permanent `wiki/qa/[slug].md` entry — so the synthesis compounds next time.

Scope: global skill, installed once at `~/.agents/skills/brain-search/SKILL.md` and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/brain-search`). Paths resolve at call time via `npx claude-second-brain path` and `npx claude-second-brain qmd` — both read `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml` to find the default brain. Source: [template/.claude/skills/brain-search/SKILL.md](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/blob/main/template/.claude/skills/brain-search/SKILL.md).

<!-- Source: /skills/brain-refresh -->

# /brain-refresh

Refresh the qmd index.

Re-scans all collections for new or changed files and regenerates vector embeddings. Run after a bulk ingest session or manual edits to the wiki.

Pass `force` to re-embed every chunk — useful after changing the embedding model.

Scope: global skill, installed once at `~/.agents/skills/brain-refresh/SKILL.md` and symlinked into each selected agent's global skills dir (e.g. `~/.claude/skills/brain-refresh`). Paths resolve at call time via `npx claude-second-brain path` and `npx claude-second-brain qmd` — both read `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml` to find the default brain. Source: [template/.claude/skills/brain-refresh/SKILL.md](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/blob/main/template/.claude/skills/brain-refresh/SKILL.md).

<!-- Source: /skills/brain-rebuild -->

# /brain-rebuild

**Destructive.** Redesign the qmd schema from scratch.

Use only when the current collection/context structure no longer fits how you search — for example, when the wiki has grown into new domains that deserve their own collections.

What it does:

1. Analyzes the current wiki.
2. Proposes new collections and contexts.
3. **Waits for your approval** before any destructive action.
4. Patches `scripts/qmd/setup.ts`, drops the old index, and rebuilds embeddings from scratch.

Scope: vault-local, installed at `.claude/skills/brain-rebuild/SKILL.md` and copied into each other selected agent's project skills dir (e.g. `.agents/skills/brain-rebuild`). Source: [template/.claude/skills/brain-rebuild/SKILL.md](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/blob/main/template/.claude/skills/brain-rebuild/SKILL.md).

<!-- Source: /skills/lint -->

# /lint

Health-check the wiki.

Reports on:

* **Orphan pages** — wiki pages with no inbound `[[links]]`.
* **Unresolved contradictions** — pages with `[!WARNING] Contradiction` callouts that haven't been resolved.
* **Stale claims** — claims superseded by newer sources.
* **Missing pages** — concepts/entities referenced by `[[links]]` that lack their own page.
* **Broken links** — wikilinks pointing to files that don't exist.
* **Data gaps** — important topics that lack source coverage; suggests specific sources to investigate.

Applies fixes where safe and flags everything else for your review. Appends a summary to `wiki/log.md`.

Scope: vault-local, installed at `.claude/skills/lint/SKILL.md` and copied into each other selected agent's project skills dir (e.g. `.agents/skills/lint`). Source: [template/.claude/skills/lint/SKILL.md](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/blob/main/template/.claude/skills/lint/SKILL.md).

# Ship log

A running record of every released version of `claude-second-brain` on npm. Newest releases first. For auto-generated notes and tags, see the [GitHub releases](https://github.com/jessepinkman9900/claude-second-brain/releases) page.

## v1.2.3 — 2026-11-27

Bug fixes for CLI argument handling, plus a test suite.

**Fixes:**

* Brain names are validated before scaffolding. Names that are empty, `.` / `..`, or contain path separators, quotes or control characters are rejected, so a name can no longer escape `~/.claude-second-brain/` or corrupt `config.toml`.
* `--brain` now requires a value in `path`, `qmd`, `exec`, `skills` and `git-token`. Previously a bare `--brain` silently fell back to the default brain (so `csb git-token --brain` renewed the wrong brain's token).
* `csb exec … -- <cmd> --help` and `csb qmd … -- … --help` now pass `--help` through to the command after `--` instead of printing csb's own help.

**Tests and CI:**

* New `pnpm test` (`node --test tests/*.test.js`) covering brain-name validation, `--brain` parsing and help pass-through; a Test workflow runs it on pull requests and `main`.

**Docs:**

* README and docs home link `/brain-ingest`, `/brain-search`, `/brain-refresh`, `/brain-rebuild` and `/lint` to their docs pages.

## v1.2.2 — 2026-11-27

npm package metadata only. No CLI or template changes.

* Added npm `keywords` matching the GitHub repo topics (`ai`, `amp`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `cursor`, `github`, `knowledge-base`, `knowledge-graph`, `knowledge-management`, `llm`, `obsidian`, `obsidian-vault`, `qmd`, `second-brain`) so the package is searchable on npmjs.com.
* npm `homepage` now points to the [docs site](https://jessepinkman9900.github.io/claude-second-brain) instead of the GitHub README, and `bugs` links to GitHub issues.

## v1.2.1 — 2026-11-27

Maintenance release: security updates and a tokenless release pipeline. No CLI or template changes.

**Security:**

* Refreshed dependencies to clear all Dependabot alerts (`pnpm audit`: 106 → 0). `@clack/prompts` is now `^1.9.0`; transitive docs-site deps (hono, vite, mermaid, dompurify, …) resolve to patched versions, with pnpm overrides for `toml`, `katex` and `@hono/node-server`.
* Removed the stale `package-lock.json`; the repo uses pnpm only.

**Release pipeline:**

* npm releases use [trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers) (OIDC) from `release-publish.yml` with `--provenance`, so no `NPM_TOKEN` is stored in the repo. npm comes from `mise.toml` (11.21.2; trusted publishing needs 11.5.1+). v1.2.0 was the first release published this way.

**CI:**

* Docs workflows install Playwright browsers from the locked version (1.65.1).

## v1.2.0 — 2026-11-27

Works with any agent, not just Claude Code, plus a faster, unattended setup and first-class Cloudflare Artifacts git tokens. Existing installs: run `csb skills` once to move global skills from `~/.claude/skills` to `~/.agents/skills` (the old copies become symlinks).

**Agents:**

* Skills install for any [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) agent, with the same layout as `npx skills`: global skills are written once to `~/.agents/skills/<name>` and symlinked into agent-specific dirs (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills`, `~/.config/goose/skills`, …). Supported: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, Amp, Cline, Windsurf, Goose, Kiro CLI, Roo Code, Continue, Junie, Augment.
* Vault-local skills (`brain-rebuild`, `lint`) are copied into each selected agent's project skills dir (`.agents/skills/`, `.windsurf/skills/`, …).
* New `--agent, -a <ids>` (comma-separated or `all`) and `CSB_AGENTS` to pick agents; `--copy` to copy instead of symlink. Interactive setup preselects Claude Code plus every detected agent.
* New `csb skills [--agent <ids>] [--copy] [--brain <name>]` to add agents or update skills later, and `csb skills --list` to show supported agents and their skills dirs.
* New vaults ship an `AGENTS.md` that points Codex, Cursor, Copilot and other agents at `CLAUDE.md`.
* The **Next steps** box shows how to open each agent you picked (`claude`, `codex`, `cursor .`, …).

**Setup:**

* All prompts, including the qmd-registration question, are asked up front; the rest runs unattended.
* Long steps show a live spinner with elapsed time and the latest output line.
* If `pnpm` 10+ is on your `PATH`, it's used directly; otherwise the CLI installs mise and fetches node + pnpm. `CSB_USE_MISE=1` forces mise.
* The git-remote picker shows GitHub / Cloudflare logos as Nerd Font glyphs in Ghostty, WezTerm and kitty, emoji elsewhere. Override with `CSB_ICONS=nerd|emoji|none`.
* If the remote can't be created or pushed, the brain is still created locally, the problem and fix are listed in **Next steps**, and the CLI exits 1.

**Cloudflare Artifacts:**

* Switched to the account-scoped REST API (`api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/<ACCOUNT_ID>/artifacts/…`); the old `artifacts.cloudflare.net/v1/api` host is no longer used. Set `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` when your login can see more than one account.
* A deleted or inactive namespace is recreated automatically before the repo is created.
* Setup now saves a 90-day git token in the vault's `.git/config` (`http.<remote>.extraHeader`), so `git push` / `git pull` and obsidian-git just work. No more 24-hour token to copy.
* New `csb git-token [<name>] [--ttl <duration>] [--read] [--print]` renews it (default 90 days, max 1 year), replacing the manual `curl` renewal.

**Other:**

* `csb doctor` accepts system pnpm 10+ in place of mise and checks that the global skills in `~/.agents/skills` match the installed release.
* README, docs and package description say "any agent" and "git" (GitHub, Cloudflare Artifacts, or any remote) instead of Claude Code and GitHub only.
* "Claude reads it" and similar wording is now agent-neutral, and "Access from anywhere" covers any local or cloud agent and any git host.

## v1.1.0 — 2026-04-19

CLI UX pass. Every addition is non-breaking — the `--` in `csb qmd -- …` and the `path --qmd` / `--config` / `--root` flag form continue to work, with a stderr deprecation notice on the flag form.

**CLI:**

* Added `csb use <name>` (aliases `default`, `switch`) to set the default brain without editing `~/.claude-second-brain/config.toml`. Runs the same header-rewrite path as `csb rm`.
* Added `csb exec [--brain <name>] -- <cmd…>` — runs any command inside the resolved brain's directory with `INDEX_PATH` pre-set. `csb qmd` now delegates to the same helper.
* Added `csb doctor` — checks for `gh` (+ auth), `mise`, `wrangler`, the central config, each brain's `path` and `qmd_index`, and whether the default brain resolves. Prints a `Fix:` hint under each failed check.
* `csb path` now accepts positional subcommands: `csb path [qmd|config|root]`. The `--qmd` / `--config` / `--root` flag form still works with a stderr deprecation warning.
* Every subcommand routes `--help` / `-h` to its own topic help. `csb help <command>` also prints per-command help. Top-level help shows the config path and current default brain.
* `csb rm` gained `--delete-remote` and `--keep-remote` for scripting. Under `-y` with neither flag, remotes are preserved (safe default).
* `resolveBrain()` error now points to `csb use <name>` as the fix.

## v1.0.0 — 2026-04-19

First major release. Brains now live at `~/.claude-second-brain/<name>/` (not the repo root), and global skills resolve paths at call time via new CLI subcommands instead of baked-in paths. Existing single-brain installs: re-run `npx claude-second-brain <name>` to migrate. Legacy `active = …` in `config.toml` is auto-rewritten to `default = …`.

**CLI:**

* Added `claude-second-brain path [--brain N] [--root|--qmd|--config]` and `claude-second-brain qmd [--brain N] -- …` subcommands. The global skills now resolve paths at call time via these commands instead of having absolute paths baked in at scaffold time.
* Added `claude-second-brain rm [<name>…]` with multi-select (space to toggle) and a follow-up prompt to delete the git remote.
* `config.toml`'s `active` field renamed to `default`. Existing configs with `active = …` are still read transparently and rewritten to `default = …` on the next write.
* Global skills (`brain-ingest`, `brain-search`, `brain-refresh`) now ship with a `.csb-version` sidecar file. Re-running `npx claude-second-brain <name>` detects version mismatches and prompts before overwriting; `CSB_SKIP_SKILL_UPDATES=1` disables the prompt.
* `npx claude-second-brain` now auto-registers qmd collections during scaffold — no manual `/setup` step needed afterwards.
* Added `csb` as a bin alias. After `npm i -g claude-second-brain`, both `claude-second-brain` and `csb` are available globally.

**Skills:**

* Removed `/setup` and `/qmd-cli` — their responsibilities are absorbed by `create.js` (auto-registration) and `/brain-refresh` / the `csb qmd` proxy respectively.
* Added `/update-workflows` to audit `pack-test.yml` drift against current repo state.
* Split `/release` into `/package-release` (version bump + PR) and an orchestrator `/release` that additionally runs `/update-workflows` and `/update-docs`.

**Refactors:**

* Removed the `__QMD_PATH__` and `__CSB_CONFIG__` placeholder substitutions. `scripts/qmd/{setup,reindex}.ts` now compute the index path from `import.meta.url`; CLAUDE.md and vault-local skills use a relative `.qmd/index.sqlite` path.
* `patchVault()` now only substitutes `__BRAIN_NAME__` in `template/README.md`. Global skills ship unmodified from the template.

**Fixes:**

* `writeConfig()` now writes `default = …` when upserting into a pre-existing empty or default-less `config.toml`. Previously a zero-byte `config.toml` blocked the field from being written and left CLI subcommands unable to resolve a default brain.
* `pnpm qmd:setup` failures during scaffolding now surface captured stderr (last ~10 lines) instead of a generic "failed" message.
* `template/scripts/qmd/{setup,reindex}.ts` wrap their bodies in `try/catch` that prints a tagged error with vault + db paths and exits 1, replacing silent unhandled rejections.
* `resolveBrain()` errors now list available brain names and include a fix hint.

**Docs:**

* Getting-started, per-skill docs, and vocs sidebar updated to reflect the 5-skill surface (`brain-ingest`, `brain-search`, `brain-refresh`, `brain-rebuild`, `lint`).
* Documented `rm` multi-select and remote-deletion prompts.
* `/setup` skill reference removed from quick-start in favor of `pnpm qmd:reindex`.

## v0.6.0 — 2026-04-17

**Features:**

* Added Cloudflare Artifacts as an alternate Git remote option during `npx claude-second-brain` setup. The CLI authenticates via wrangler, creates a repo via the Artifacts API, and pushes the initial commit automatically.

**CLI UX:**

* qmd index path prompt now appears before the Git remote selection.
* Global Claude skills are installed right after `pnpm install`, before git init. Install path is shown with `~/...` notation.
* qmd index prompt placeholder and default value display `~/...` instead of the full home directory path.

**Docs:**

* Added a **Git backends** section to the docs site covering GitHub and Cloudflare Artifacts setup.
* Added `llms.txt` for LLM/AI crawler discoverability.
* Docs site now generates `.md` files alongside HTML pages.

**Refactors:**

* Unified every qmd path reference behind the `__QMD_PATH__` placeholder and parallelized file patching during scaffold.
* CLI version is now read from `package.json` instead of being hardcoded.

**Fixes:**

* Resolved a batch of code smells and factual inconsistencies across the codebase.
* `patchVault` now surfaces non-`ENOENT` errors instead of swallowing them.
* Fixed a failing CI job.

**Docs:**

* Added a unified mermaid architecture diagram to both READMEs.
* Removed generic skills-marketplace boilerplate.

* Added a GitHub repo creation prompt during `npx claude-second-brain` (with a private-repo notice and a fallback that removes the repo on failure).
* The generated README title now matches the brain folder name.
* Polished the CLI UX with `@clack/prompts` and now runs `mise trust` before installing dependencies.

**Docs:**

* Updated READMEs to reflect the new CLI prompts and skill renames.

**Chore:**

* Removed template skills from `.claude/skills`.
